title: How to run and score a mock interview

kcs.statement: A mock interview is scored against a fixed rubric: requirements, estimates, API, data model, high-level design, deep dive and bottlenecks. Each area is marked present, partial or missing.
A mock counts only when one uninterrupted 45-minute attempt produces a submitted answer covering all seven rubric areas; scoring happens afterwards in separate review time, not during the 45 minutes.
After each mock, the learner compares their timeline against the 45-minute budget and writes down the one area that overran or was skipped as the target for the next mock.

problem_ideas: Score a sample transcript that spent 20 minutes on requirements and never reached bottlenecks.
Allocate 45 minutes across the seven rubric areas and defend the split.
Rewrite a vague answer ('we'll add caching') into a rubric-complete statement.
List three clarifying questions that would change the design of a feed.
Spot the missing area in a short written answer to 'design Pastebin'.
A learner paused at minute 20 to look up a formula. Decide whether the attempt counts and what to change next time.
Pick the next practice target from three past rubric sheets.
